q1_issues.issue: "them" has no antecedent and no human-only predicate or role, so typing the witness group `person` violates the explicit bar on reading `person` off a plural pronoun alone — the fallback kind is required.
The second clause's "them" witness carries the same unlicensed `person` typing.
"immediately" is a temporal adverb, not a how-adverb of manner, so `(Manner sk_make_1 immediately)` asserts a manner the sentence does not state (repeated inside the rule at statement 10).
The maintenance verb "keep them sealed" reifies the state and links `Result` but omits the required `(Still sk_sealed_1)` continuation marker.

q2_gaps: an adverb of immediacy ("immediately") has no licensed slot — the instructions rule `Manner` out for sequence/ordering adverbs and supply no alternative carrier, so the adverbial can only be dropped and recorded
notes: Resolving "others" to a second `state` group off the parallel first clause is well supported by the text, which sharpens the contrast with the unsupported `person` typing of "them"; the fresh-witness-per-clause treatment of the contrastive "some … others …" pair is exactly per doctrine. Hanging the 30-year bound on the sealed state rather than the keep event is defensible, since a state is an eventuality too.
